newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peru rebel hostage-takers refuse exile - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel hostage-takers refuse exile - spokesman.

text.p: Peruvian MRTA rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima will not accept exile, a spokesman for the group said on Monday.
"We are not thinking about leaving Peru," spokesman Isaac Velasco told reporters in Pamplona, Spain where he was attending a book presentation.
"We have expressed our decision to stay in Peru because we are Peruvians. Peru is in a very serious crisis which we are part of and we want to be part of the solution," he added.
About 20 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels have been holding the hostages for 76 days at the diplomatic residence.

Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori went to Cuba and the Dominican Republic on Monday to discuss the crisis. News reports have identified Cuba, Nicaragua or a country in Eastern Europe as potential places of asylum for the rebels.

While ruling out the main demand of the rebels -- the release of 400 jailed comrades -- Fujimori has indicated he might make other concessions. He has always left the way open to asylum in another country for the rebels.
